title: The workload of the early years
summary: Bigard says they worked clubs, records, films, jukebox shorts and after-hours dances, all happily until greed took over.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: You know people don't seem to realize that we used to work so much, I mean, sometimes we had two or three jobs at one time we were working. We was working the club, then we would record -- we would make -- we'd be making a movie and then we used to make those little -- they had things that -- they don't have them anymore, like on the juke box there, little movies, of the different clubs and we'd make those things. We used to make little recordings for -- they called it a weekly, recording, for they call it a weekly recording, like little paper things, you remember that?

Yeah, paper, say they'd sell for ten or 15 cents on the newsstands. All them kind of things. And we used to play at after hour dances, and all that. But ain't nobody -- you know -- they didn't complain about all the work, they were happy doing it. Until all the greed, when the greed start coming in they found out that well they can get the name now, they can make the money without getting
it all distributed among the boys then things began to fall apart. And that was it. But --
